ProfileHub.faqQ_track: How do I track a delivery?
ProfileHub.faqA_track: Profile → Orders shows each order's carrier, delivery stage and expected date. Open an order for its full timeline and tracking link.
ProfileHub.faqQ_fgas: Do I need an F-Gas certificate to order?
ProfileHub.faqA_fgas: Yes, for fluorinated refrigerants — tools and accessories don't need one. Upload your certificate in Profile → F-Gas & CO₂e; it is checked automatically and then applies to every order until it expires.
ProfileHub.faqQ_vat: Where does my VAT ID appear?
ProfileHub.faqA_vat: Add your EU VAT ID (or ЄДРПОУ) in Profile → Edit profile. It is printed on every invoice. For questions about VAT treatment of a specific order, ask in the support chat.
ProfileHub.faqQ_address: Can I change the delivery address after ordering?
ProfileHub.faqA_address: Ask in the support chat with your order number. Our logistics team can change the delivery site until the order is dispatched.
ProfileHub.faqQ_cylinders: How do I return empty cylinders?
ProfileHub.faqA_cylinders: Profile → Cylinders & deposits → Request a return. Choose collection from one of your addresses or drop-off at our warehouse; the deposit is refunded once the cylinders arrive.

MarketHub.why_carFlammable: R-290 is class A3 (highly flammable) — not permitted in vehicle A/C, which is designed for A1 / A2L gases.
MarketHub.why_carPressure: {p} bar g at +45 °C — {ratio}× the {ref} bar g of {base} that a car circuit (hoses, condenser, compressor) is built for. Stationary HFC with POE oil, not PAG: not suitable.
MarketHub.why_carDowngrade: Not allowed: a car built for R-1234yf may not be refilled with a GWP > 150 gas such as R-134a (Directive 2006/40/EC), and the service ports differ.
MarketHub.why_carUpgrade: Only an R-134a car could take R-1234yf, and that is not an approved retrofit — it needs the maker’s procedure, A2L-rated parts and new labels.
MarketHub.why_flammable: R-290 (A3) needs a system designed for hydrocarbons — never a drop-in for an HFC system.
MarketHub.why_tooLowPressure: A much lower-pressure gas ({p} vs {ref} bar g at +45 °C): capacity collapses and the oil/expansion device are wrong — not a substitute.
MarketHub.why_notInterchangeable: Different pressure ({p} vs {ref} bar g at +45 °C for {base}) and blend composition — not interchangeable without a re-engineered system.
MarketHub.why_chillerYf: R-1234yf is not a drop-in for an R-134a chiller (A2L, lower capacity); the lower-GWP route for R-134a chillers is R-513A.

MarketHub.dxWhy_normal: Evaporating ~7 °C, condensing ~15 K above ambient, superheat 5–8 K and subcooling 5–8 K: a healthy system.
MarketHub.dxWhy_undercharge: Low pressures on both sides, high superheat (the evaporator runs out of liquid) and almost no subcooling: not enough refrigerant — find the leak, then charge by weight.
MarketHub.dxWhy_overcharge: High head pressure, high subcooling (liquid backed up in the condenser) and low superheat: too much refrigerant. Recover to the nameplate charge.
MarketHub.dxWhy_condenserAirflow: High condensing temperature with normal subcooling and superheat: the charge is fine but heat isn’t leaving — dirty coil, blocked airflow or a failed fan.
MarketHub.dxWhy_restriction: Very low suction, high superheat AND high subcooling: refrigerant is held back before the evaporator — a blocked filter-drier or a starving TXV (the frost marks the restriction).
MarketHub.dxWhy_evapAirflow: Low suction pressure but LOW superheat: the evaporator isn’t getting heat — dirty filter, slow fan or an iced coil. Not a charge problem.
MarketHub.dxWhy_compressorWeak: Suction high and discharge low (small pressure ratio) with normal-ish superheat: the compressor isn’t pumping — worn valves or internal bypass.
MarketHub.q_mac150: Since 1 January 2017, new EU vehicles must use an A/C refrigerant with GWP below…
MarketHub.q_mac150_why: Directive 2006/40/EC (MAC): GWP < 150 for all new vehicles from 2017 — in practice R-1234yf (GWP 4) or R-744.
MarketHub.q_service2500: From 1 January 2025, servicing refrigeration with VIRGIN gas of GWP ≥ 2500 is banned. Which gas does this hit?
MarketHub.q_service2500_why: R-404A has GWP 3922. Reg. (EU) 2024/573 Art. 13 allows only reclaimed or recycled gas of GWP ≥ 2500 for servicing (refrigeration until 2030).
MarketHub.q_r32class_why: A2L: lower toxicity, mildly flammable — like R-1234yf. Charge limits and A2L-rated tools apply.
MarketHub.q_r290class_why: A3: lower toxicity, highly flammable — systems must be designed for hydrocarbons.
MarketHub.q_carOil: Which oil family do belt-driven car A/C compressors (R-134a / R-1234yf) use?
MarketHub.q_carOil_why: PAG (polyalkylene glycol). Stationary HFC systems use POE — mixing them up damages compressors.
MarketHub.q_splitOil: Which oil family is used with R-410A in split systems?
MarketHub.q_splitOil_why: POE (polyolester), miscible with HFCs. Mineral oil (MO) belongs to old CFC/HCFC systems.
MarketHub.q_superheat_a: suction-line temperature minus evaporating saturation temperature
MarketHub.q_superheat_b: condensing saturation temperature minus liquid-line temperature
MarketHub.q_superheat_why: Measured at the evaporator outlet / suction line: how far the vapour is above its boiling point. It protects the compressor from liquid.
MarketHub.q_subcooling_a: suction-line temperature minus evaporating saturation temperature
MarketHub.q_subcooling_c: condensing saturation temperature minus liquid-line temperature
MarketHub.q_subcooling_why: Measured at the condenser outlet: how far the liquid is below its condensing point — the main charge check on TXV systems.
MarketHub.q_pressure45: Which gas has the highest saturation pressure at +45 °C?
MarketHub.q_pressure45_why: R-32: about {r32} bar g, versus about {r134a} bar g for R-134a — why stationary high-pressure gases can never go into a car circuit.
MarketHub.q_quota2050: Under Annex VII of Reg. 2024/573, the EU HFC quota in 2050 is… (t CO₂e)
MarketHub.q_quota2050_why: Zero: placing HFCs on the EU market ends in 2050.
MarketHub.q_r404nbp_why: About −46 °C (bubble point) — a low-temperature gas, used in freezers and cold rooms.
MarketHub.q_split750: From which year are new single split A/C units under 3 kg with GWP ≥ 750 banned?
MarketHub.q_split750_why: 2025 (Reg. 2024/573 Annex IV) — which is why new small splits use R-32 (GWP 675) or lower.
MarketHub.q_quotaHalf: The EU HFC quota for 2027–2029 is what share of 2025–2026?
